step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify end user consumer (USERS -> UserConsumerWeb) initiating URL requests to CloudFront.
2. CloudFront triggers Lambda@Edge, which queries DynamoDB to retrieve target destination URLs and return them to users.
3. CloudFront logs are sent to an S3 bucket (raw logs), transformed by a Lambda function, sent to Kinesis Data Firehose, and stored in a second S3 bucket (processed logs).
4. Admin staff (ADMIN -> UserCompanyDeveloper) access the system via API Gateway and an administrative Lambda function.
5. The Admin Lambda manages short URLs in DynamoDB, user permissions in RDS (Aurora), and executes analytical queries via Athena against processed log data in S3.
6. AWS Glue optimizes data in the processed S3 log bucket for Athena queries.
